instructions.en: On each trial you will see a short list of digits — try to remember them. After a brief pause a single digit appears. Press YES if that digit was in the list, and NO if it was not. Answer as fast as you can while staying accurate.
instructions.he: בכל ניסיון תוצג רשימה קצרה של ספרות — נסו לזכור אותה. אחרי הפסקה קצרה תופיע ספרה בודדת. הקישו כן אם הספרה הייתה ברשימה, ולא אם לא הייתה. ענו מהר ככל האפשר תוך שמירה על דיוק.

simplifications.what: The memory set is shown all at once instead of one digit at a time at 1.2s each, with study time kept proportional at 800ms per digit.
simplifications.why: A variable-length sequence of displays is not expressible — the phase list is fixed for every trial. Proportional exposure preserves per-item encoding time, and the set-size effect on retrieval RT is robust to simultaneous presentation, which is how many modern replications run it.

simplifications.what: Set sizes 1, 2, 4 and 6 with three fixed digit sets each, rather than a fresh random series of length 1-6 on every trial.
simplifications.why: Keeps every cell balanced and the session classroom-sized; three variants per size stop a single set being learned across trials.

simplifications.what: The recall-the-series-in-order step after each response was dropped.
simplifications.why: It checked that the set was still held; it costs time and the reaction-time effect does not depend on it.

simplifications.what: Inter-trial gap of 1s rather than the paper's 3.7s.
simplifications.why: The gap separates trials; its length does not affect the scanning result.
